module: Manager of the rally co-driver's audio queue. It queues 'audioObj's (note clips, system notes, pauses) and plays them one by one via Engine.Audio.intercomPlayPacenote, respecting each clip's duration plus a configurable spacing (between corners, phrases, link words and notes). The spacings come from the active voicepack's entry and are bounded by gameplay_rally_audioTiming. The module returns a constructor: require(...)(rallyManager). onUpdate must be called every frame.
usage:
local am = require('/lua/ge/extensions/gameplay/rally/audioManager')(rallyManager)
am:enqueuePacenoteAudio(pacenote)
-- every frame:
am:onUpdate(dtReal, dtSim, dtRaw)
notes: The audioLen and timeouts durations are in seconds; the gaps are in milliseconds and can be negative (overlap).
A clip has a minimum effective duration of 0.01 s.
An audioObj can carry audioCandidates: a candidate is then drawn at random (math.random) at queuing time.
An audio channel is forcibly stopped after audioLen + 0.25 s (audioStopGraceSecs) if it has not finished.
A pause (audioType='pause') plays no sound, it simply blocks the queue for audioLen seconds.
enqueueSystemPacenote: the 'else' error test reads pacenote.name while pacenote is nil: crash if nil is passed.
C:_loadPacenoteMetadata is empty; pacenoteMetadataOfflineStructured and pacenoteMetadataOnlineStructuredAndFreeform stay nil.

C.desc: Audio manager returned by the module constructor. Attributes: rallyManager, queue (dequeue), currAudioObj, activeAudioChannels, cornerGapMs, phraseGapMs, linkWordGapMs, pacenoteGapMs, enableSpeedScaling, codriverTimingOffsetSeconds.

init.desc: Initializes the state (empty queue, spacings at 0) then loads the timing settings of the active voicepack of the rallyManager's notebook.

rallyManager.desc: Rally manager; its notebook field (method resolveActiveVoicepack) provides the voicepack.

_loadVoicepackTimingDefaults.desc: Resolves the notebook's active voicepack (notebook:resolveActiveVoicepack) and applies its settings via setVoicepackTiming.

setVoicepackTiming.desc: Applies a voicepack's settings: cornerGapMs, phraseGapMs, linkWordGapMs (default = phraseGapMs), pacenoteGapMs, enableSpeedScaling (true unless equal to false) and codriverTimingOffsetSeconds. Without an entry, everything is 0 and speed scaling is active.

getCornerGapMs.desc: Gap (ms) between two consecutive corner clips.

setCornerGapMs.desc: Sets the gap between corners (bounded by audioTiming.clampCornerGapMs).

getPhraseGapMs.desc: Gap (ms) between two phrases (clips) of the same note.

getLinkWordGapMs.desc: Gap (ms) applied after a link word (clip of category 'linkword').

setLinkWordGapMs.desc: Sets the gap after a link word (bounded).

getPacenoteGapMs.desc: Gap (ms) between the end of one note and the next.

isSpeedScalingEnabled.desc: Indicates whether the co-driver's delay depends on speed (true unless the voicepack disabled it).

getCodriverTimingOffsetSeconds.desc: Voicepack-specific co-driver timing offset, in seconds.

_getAudioObjGapAfterMs.desc: Gap to apply after a clip: linkWordGap for the 'linkword' category; if structuredTimingAfter=='clip', cornerGap between two consecutive 'corner' clips otherwise phraseGap; if 'pacenote', pacenoteGap; otherwise 0.

_audioObjEffectiveLen.desc: Single source of a clip's playback duration, trailing gap included: max(audioLen + gap/1000, 0.01).

pacenoteEffectiveAudioLen.desc: Total spoken duration of a note: sum of the effective durations of its clips minus the note's end gap (that is spacing toward the next note, not the end of the note).

returns.desc: Duration in seconds (0 if no clips).

resetQueue.desc: Clears the queue, stops all ongoing audio channels and forgets the current clip.

_trackAudioChannel.desc: Stores an active audio channel and its expiry time (rallyUtil.getTime) for automatic stopping; ignores a non-numeric identifier.

_stopExpiredAudioChannels.desc: Stops (Engine.Audio.intercomStopPacenote) the channels whose expiry time has passed and recomputes the next expiry.

_stopAudio.desc: Immediately stops all active audio channels.

handleDamage.desc: If a note without the 'damage' flag is playing on an active channel, cuts it, clears the queue and forgets the clip: the interrupted note will not be replayed.

enqueuePauseSecs.desc: Adds a silent pause to the queue (used at the start and finish lines).

addToFront.desc: true to place at the head of the queue.
true to insert at the head.

returns.desc: Number of clips processed (0 if nil).

enqueuePacenoteAudio.desc: Queues all clips of a note (pacenote:audioObjs()). Logs an error if there are no clips.

addToFront.desc: true to insert at the head.

enqueueSystemPacenote.desc: Queues a system note (audio file audioFname). If the file is missing, shows an error message on screen and does nothing. The default duration is 1.0 s.

addToFront.desc: true to insert at the head.

audioLen.desc: Clip duration in seconds (1.0 by default).

_enqueueAudioObj.desc: Adds a clip to the queue (head or tail). If the clip has audioCandidates, draws one at random and copies its fname/audioLen.

isPlaying.desc: True as long as the current clip (or pause) has not reached its timeout.

returns.desc: true if playback is in progress.

getQueueInfo.desc: Returns a reused table {queueSize, paused}; paused is true when nothing is playing. The table is shared between calls: do not keep it.

playNextInQueue.desc: If nothing is playing, removes the next clip from the queue: for a note, starts Engine.Audio.intercomPlayPacenote (file pacenoteFname) and computes the timeout; for a pause, only computes the timeout. Ignores notes without a file name.

onUpdate.desc: Called every frame: stops expired channels, then starts the next clip if possible.
